chapter: Chicago, the Woodside, the army and 52nd Street
title: Life at the Woodside: Harold West's cooking and rehearsing with Lester
summary: Residents pooled money for groceries, and the group rehearsed with Prez and Shad Collins until Hammond's Billie Holiday plan broke it up.

story.theme_name: Lester Young: the man, the sound, the Basie years
story.community_name: Remembering Lester Young: Prez the man and his sound

blocks.x: Who lived in the Woodside then?
Well, Butter lived on the first floor, and all of the Erskine Hawkins band lived there. And Lester of course --
I don't remember Butter. No, I don't remember eating of his
Butter always had good cooks around him.

Yeah, yeah. Yeah, well that's evident by size, you know. But Harold was a marvelous cook, and so we would just pool our money and give Harold -- we would buy the groceries and Harold would cook, you know. And this -- I think this is why -- this is how we started rehearsing together, Lester, Harold, and Shad Collins used to come around all the time. And when they -- Shad had played with Basie also, and we got a bass player by the name of Nick Fenton, as I told you, and this is how we started rehearsing. We just rehearsed this group down here and John Hammond at this time was interested, still interested in Prez. But as I told you
before, in the back of his mind he had -- he wanted Prez to be the backup for Billie Holliday. And when Prez found this out he refused.
